_comment: The How to Play page, opened from the title screen and the system menu. One section per heading; each line is a paragraph. Source text: README, 'Playing the vertical slice'.
title: How to Play

sections.heading: Walking
lines: WASD or the arrow keys walk the ground. Walk off its edge and the party steps on across the continent; every step advances the world clock.
The line at the bottom always says what you can do where you stand: in a town, H hires, B buys and J reads the board, without leaving the street.

N opens the journal, and the map is in it: the continent, black where you have never been. Esc puts the map away. Its first page, The Company, is a sheet for each companion: every number, and what a level adds.
Esc opens the menu: save, load, sound, fullscreen and these pages. F11 switches fullscreen anywhere.
Q hands the run to the game and T cycles the speed — on the road, inside a town and in a fight alike. Q again takes it back.

sections.heading: Danger
lines: Danger is a property of place. Near an open gate the wild is thick with what came out of it; near a hearth it goes quiet. Roughly 37% per step in a gate's mouth against 1% at home.
Gates never reopen once shut — but one left standing open too long breaks, and what was behind it comes out levelled up.
A gate left open puts the nearest settlement under siege. Walk in while it is happening and V fights the besiegers off. Leave it too long and the town falls.

sections.heading: Sites
lines: On the map: green dots are villages, grey keeps, blue libraries, tan huts, red gates (a ring means open and spilling), gold is the Tower, and the orange roof is home.
Walk into a village, keep or hut to rest. H hires whoever is drinking there, B buys the gear on the shelf, J reads the job board, Y opens the Adventurers Guild where there is one.
A library teaches whoever has not read its book. An open gate is a fight — and once inside there is no walking out until it is beaten or you are.
Home is your own doorstep: nothing camps within sight of it, sleeping there always patches the party up, and U buys a better bed for permanent extra HP.
Word of what you do travels outward from where you did it, about a tile every fourteen steps, and sets what towns call you and what they charge.

sections.heading: Battle
lines: Fights run in real time and open paused. Space pauses and unpauses, and orders can be given while paused. T changes the speed; Z sets when the fight pauses itself.

Left-click picks a fighter, or drag a box to pick several; 1–6 pick one and Tab picks everyone. Right-click the ground to move, an enemy to attack, a fallen friend to help them up. Q W E R ready a skill, then click its target.

Everyone swings on their own; A switches a fighter's skills between automatic and by hand, and H holds them where they stand. Skills come back on cooldowns and cost energy; a tired fighter only swings.
Facing matters. The wedge on a token shows where it looks: side hits deal 1.1×, back hits 1.2×.
Draughts and herbs are on each fighter's card. One takes a moment to use, and what is used is gone from the stores.

sections.heading: Characters and death
lines: Falling is usually fatal. A downed character can be helped up for a few seconds; after that they roll their graces — a charm carried, an ally still standing, a book they read, the ground they fell on — and dies if none of them land. Raiders may take them alive instead; R ransoms them, F takes them back by force.
The run follows you, not the party. Companions can all die and the story goes on; when your own character falls, it stops. Hire replacements in towns.
Experience comes from the first of each kind. A kind of enemy teaches whoever kills it first, once. The way to grow is to go and meet something new.
Level 2 is a choice. When someone is ready the bottom line says so — press P and pick their class.

sections.heading: The Tower
lines: The Tower is ten floors, each paying gold, a book every third and a generated skill tree every fourth, up to the Spire Archon on floor 10.
Gold won on the Tower is a hoard you carry. Walking off its step banks it; losing a floor leaves it behind. Every extra floor is a decision about what you are already holding.

sections.heading: The party screen
lines: P opens the party screen, where the run is managed: pick a class from its card, teach a book to someone who lacks it, and see what each character has read and what is close to fading. On the Powers page a glowing stone is a power you can take; press it.
The Training Yoke trades 25% of attack for 50% more experience. The Practice page sends a companion off to walk an errand while you walk.
It also shows the Codex — how much of the world's power grammar has been catalogued. N opens the journal.
